html:
The University of Coimbra is one of the oldest universities in the world still running. It was founded by King Denis in Lisbon in 1290 and settled for good in Coimbra in 1537.

For most of its history it was the only university in Portugal and its empire. It trained the lawyers, priests, doctors and officials who ran Portugal and Brazil, among them leaders of Brazilian independence. The Marquis of Pombal reformed it in 1772, adding science and mathematics.

Its old buildings on the hill above the city, with the Joanina library of the 1700s, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its students' black capes and their own style of fado are famous. Compare the University of Salamanca in Spain.
